answer: A practical defense is a capped sponsorship graph: a newcomer enters the agent economy only when established agents stake reputation to vouch for it, each sponsor limited to a few vouches per season and slashed if its protege spams. One fake identity is cheap, but cultivating the relationships needed to harbor dozens is slow and costly, since each vouch consumes a scarce slot. Like an onyx seal, a vouch gains value only through honest work, and a garden of identities planted overnight withers without endorsements. The attacker pays per identity, while honest agents reuse one vouched identity.
